contests.title: City of Sterling Referred Ballot Issue 2A

provenance.quote: SHALL THE CITY OF STERLING TAXES BE INCREASED $3,600,000 ANNUALLY, BEGINNING JANUARY 1, 2027, AND BY SUCH AMOUNTS AS ARE COLLECTED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER FOR A PERIOD OF FIVE (5) YEARS, BY THE IMPOSITION OF AN ADDITIONAL TEMPORARY 1.0% CITY SALES AND USE TAX, IN ORDER TO INCREASE OR IMPROVE PUBLIC SERVICES INCLUDING STREET AND ROAD IMPROVEMENTS AND RELATED MAINTENANCE NEEDS; AND SHALL THE REVENUES FROM SUCH TAX: BE DEPOSITED INTO A DEDICATED FUND SEPARATE FROM THE CITY'S GENERAL FUND AND USED SOLELY FOR THE PURPOSE OF REPAVING, REPAIRING, MAINTAINING, AND IMPROVING CITY STREETS AND ROADS, INCLUDING RELATED IMPROVEMENTS SUCH AS DRAINAGE, CURBS AND GUTTERS, AND PEDESTRIAN SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS; AND SHALL THE CITY BE AUTHORIZED TO COLLECT, RETAIN, AND SPEND ALL REVENUES GENERATED BY SUCH TAX, TOGETHER WITH ANY EARNINGS THEREON, WITHOUT LIMITATION OR CONDITION, AS A VOTER-APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE PURSUANT TO ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION, OR ANY OTHER LAW?

contests.title: Buffalo School District RE-4J Referred Ballot Issue 5A

provenance.quote: WITHOUT IMPOSING A NEW TAX, SHALL BUFFALO SCHOOL DISTRICT RE-4J DEBT BE INCREASED $1.25 MILLION, WITH A TOTAL REPAYMENT COST OF UP TO $1.7 MILLION, AND SHALL DISTRICT TAXES AUTHORIZED IN 2007 BE EXTENDED TO PAY SUCH NEW DEBT INCURRED FOR THE PURPOSE OF FINANCING THE COSTS OF: UPGRADING AND ENHANCING SECURITY · AND SAFETY FEATURES, INCLUDING THE INSTALLATION OF NEW CAMERA AND KEY FOB ACCESS SYSTEMS; CONSTRUCTING IMPROVEMENTS TO THE · MAIN ENTRANCES OF THE ELEMENTARY AND HIGH SCHOOL BUILDINGS; AND IMPROVING THE DISTRICT'S ELEMENTARY · PLAYGROUND, INCLUDING THE INSTALLATION OF SAFER FLOORING AND OTHER UPGRADES; AND TO THE EXTENT OF AVAILABLE FUNDS, REFINANCING THE DISTRICT'S EXISTING CAPITAL LEASE, BY THE ISSUANCE AND PAYMENT OF GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS WHICH SHALL BEAR INTEREST, MATURE, BE SUBJECT TO REDEMPTION, WITH OR WITHOUT PREMIUM, AND BE ISSUED AT SUCH TIME, AT SUCH PRICE (AT, ABOVE OR BELOW PAR) AND IN SUCH MANNER AND CONTAINING SUCH TERMS CONSISTENT WITH THIS BALLOT ISSUE, AS THE BOARD OF EDUCATION MAY DETERMINE; AND SHALL AD VALOREM PROPERTY TAXES BE LEVIED WITHOUT LIMIT AS TO THE MILL RATE TO GENERATE AMOUNTS, NOT TO EXCEED $200,000 ANNUALLY, SUFFICIENT IN EACH YEAR TO PAY THE PRINCIPAL OF, PREMIUM IF ANY, AND INTEREST ON THE BONDS?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add 1 percentage point to Sterling’s sales and use taxes for five years beginning January 1, 2027. The question authorizes $3.6 million a year and the amounts the tax collects later during that period. Revenue would go to a dedicated fund separate from the city’s general fund and could be used only to repave, repair, maintain and improve city streets and roads, including drainage, curbs, gutters and pedestrian-safety improvements. Revenue and earnings could be retained and spent outside the stated constitutional and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the five-year sales and use tax for the dedicated street and road fund and its revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional sales and use tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allow the school district to borrow $1.25 million, with total repayment capped at $1.7 million, and extend property taxes approved in 2007 to repay the new debt. The property-tax rate could vary without a mill-rate ceiling, but annual repayment taxes would be capped at $200,000 and limited to amounts needed for principal, any repayment premium and interest. Money would pay for the safety and school improvements listed below and, if funds are available, refinancing the district’s existing capital lease.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the new school bonds and extension of existing repayment taxes within the stated borrowing, repayment and annual-tax limits.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this new debt or its associated extension of repayment taxes through this measure.

parts.label: School projects
parts.what: Projects are security and safety upgrades, including new camera and key-fob access systems; improvements to the main entrances of the elementary and high school buildings; and improvements to the elementary playground, including safer flooring and other upgrades. Refinancing the existing capital lease would depend on available funds.

parts.label: Bond terms
parts.what: The school board would set interest rates, maturity and issuance dates, prices above, below or equal to the bonds’ principal, and early-repayment terms with or without an extra charge, consistent with the question.
